newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Housewares shares sink on profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Housewares shares sink on profit warning.

text.p: Shares in South African mail sales business Housewares Ltd slipped on Thursday after the group published a profit-warning in the morning, dealers and analysts said.
"It is on the cautionary that we've seen some selling in Housewares today," one dealer said.
The share fell 30 cents, or 12 percent, to 220 cents in a volume of 67,400 shares valued at nearly 160,000 rand.

The company's share price has been on a downward trend since last July after its split from Education Investment Corp Ltd (Educor). It has fallen from around seven rand in July to its current level of 220 cents
"The company has been doing pretty badly since its split from Educor. By the time a company publishes a profit-warning it will be close to a low point in its share price," one analyst said.
Housewares said on Thursday that earnings per share for the current financial year would be lower than those achieved for the financial year ended March 31, 1996.
It said the rejection rate of credit applications had been greater than in the previous period and the incidence of bad debts had increased.
But analysts said losses could be overdone and the share was looking attractive in the long-term.
"It was very expensive at seven rand but now it could be cheap in the long-term," one commented.
